# Results — Study 372 (Max-Pain Pinning)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The folklore "max-pain pinning"
— that the underlying gets dragged to the **strike of maximum pain** at expiry — tested two
ways. **(1) A real option-chain snapshot:** for 20 liquid US underlyings we pull live call/put
open interest, compute each one's **max-pain strike**, and measure how far spot sits from it
*today*. yfinance retains no expiry-day history, so the snapshot can only describe *where
price sits now* — it **cannot** test the landing-at-expiry claim. **(2) A deterministic
synthetic pinning control:** many simulated (underlying, expiry) episodes with a tunable
``pin`` knob, where the truth is known. Offline & deterministic; run `python examples/verify.py`
to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance live option chains (call/put open interest per strike) + last close, 20 liquid US underlyings |
| As-of | **2026-06-22** (one cross-sectional snapshot; **PROXY**/snapshot, not a pinning panel) |
| Max-pain rule | strike minimising total option payout, `Σ max(s−K,0)·callOI + Σ max(K−s,0)·putOI` |
| What's testable here | the spot-vs-max-pain **gap today** — *not* the expiry-day landing (no history retained) |
| Synthetic control | 400 episodes/grid, ``pin`` = daily fraction of the spot→max-pain gap closed; seed 372 |

> **Snapshot caveat (named on the Signal axis).** A live option chain gives only **upcoming**
> expiries: we can compute today's max-pain but never see how those contracts *expire*. The
> landing claim ("price gets pinned to max-pain at the close") is therefore **untestable on
> this free tape** and is deferred to the synthetic control, where the pinning truth is known
> by construction. The snapshot's role is narrow but real: if price were already pinned to
> max-pain, the gaps would cluster near zero — they do not.

## The real snapshot — price is NOT sitting on max-pain

20 liquid underlyings, as-of 2026-06-22. ``gap%`` = (spot − max-pain) / spot.

| stat | value |
|---|--:|
| underlyings | **20** |
| median \|gap\| | **2.06%** |
| mean \|gap\| | **2.16%** |
| within **0.5%** of max-pain | **25%** |
| within **1.0%** of max-pain | **30%** |
| max \|gap\| (AMD) | **7.48%** |

The deep, most-liquid names (SPY −0.33%, QQQ −0.35%) sit closest — consistent with index
options being heavily arbitraged — but the cross-section's **median gap is ~2%**, and only
**3 in 10** names are even within 1% of max-pain. A genuine "pin" would put price *on* the
strike; instead the snapshot shows price scattered a couple of percent away. This is a
description, not a test of the landing claim — but it is squarely **against** the strong
folklore.

## The synthetic pinning control — the engine is honest, and the pin must be *planted*

400 episodes per grid; the **paired t** is on the per-episode difference
``dist(close, spot-anchor) − dist(close, max-pain)`` (positive ⇒ the close was pulled *toward*
max-pain and *away* from where it started). ``win`` = P[close nearer max-pain than the
spot-anchor]; ``p_plac`` = label-shuffle placebo; the fade-trade is the believer's directional
bet, 1-day lag, net of a 5-bps round-trip.

| planted ``pin`` | d→max-pain | d→spot-anchor | diff | paired *t* | win-rate | placebo *p* | fade gross | fade net | hit |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no pin) | 3.69 | 2.12 | **−1.57** | **−11.49** | 26% | 0.47 | +0.05% | −0.00% | 51% |
| 0.05 (weak) | 3.04 | 2.07 | −0.97 | −7.29 | 32% | 0.00 | +0.73% | +0.68% | 63% |
| 0.15 (moderate) | 2.15 | 2.38 | +0.23 | +1.82 | 48% | 0.00 | +1.73% | +1.68% | 75% |
| **0.40** (strong) | 1.32 | 3.08 | **+1.76** | **+14.33** | 69% | 0.00 | +2.82% | +2.77% | 86% |

Read it carefully. With **no pinning** (`pin = 0`) the paired *t* is **−11.49** and the
win-rate **26%**: the close lands *closer to where it started* than to max-pain, and the
label-shuffle placebo (*p* = **0.47**) confirms the true max-pain pins **no better than a
randomly relabelled one**. The harness **cannot** manufacture a pin out of nothing. Only when
we *plant* a strong drag (`pin = 0.40`) does the close pile onto max-pain (*t* = **+14.33**,
win **69%**) and the fade-trade earn a real **+2.8% gross / 86% hit**. The control proves two
things at once: the measurement engine is unbiased, **and** the only world where max-pain
pinning is tradable is the one where we hand-build the pin.

## Robustness — more episodes never fakes a pin

| episodes (pin = 0) | paired *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 200 | −8.46 | 0.66 |
| 400 | −11.49 | 0.47 |
| 800 | −16.35 | 0.39 |

Throwing more data at the zero-pin world only makes the *t* **more negative** — the absence of
a pin is detected ever more confidently, never inverted into a false positive. And pinning
needs *time* to act: at `pin = 0.15` the paired *t* runs **−5.12 → +1.82 → +9.59** as
days-to-expiry goes **3 → 5 → 10**, i.e. a real drag only shows once it has had days to work.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The academic literature (Ni–Pearson–Poteshman 2005; Avellaneda–Lipkin
  2003) documents a *modest, single-stock* clustering toward high-OI strikes via delta-hedging
  — so the effect is **not nothing**. But it is a *strike*-clustering tendency, not a
  *max-pain* law; on our free tape there is **no expiry-day panel to certify any pin** (snapshot
  only), and the snapshot itself shows price a **median ~2% away** from max-pain. Literature
  support + a synthetic-only positive control + a real tape that can't test the claim ⇒
  **WEAK**, never REAL (the t ≥ 2 bar is met only where we *plant* the edge).
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Even in the synthetic world the fade-trade only pays when pinning
  is *strong and planted*; in the real snapshot there is no observable pull to capture, and a
  live max-pain-fade in single names would eat expiry-day spreads, borrow on shorts, and the
  ~2% noise the snapshot shows. There is no deployable edge.
- **"Pinned"? — BUSTED.** The dramatic "the stock gets pinned to the max-pain strike" is busted
  as a general law: it is, at most, a weak single-stock tendency, is **absent in liquid index
  names**, and is contradicted by a snapshot where price sits a couple of percent off max-pain.
  Real-as-a-footnote, busted-as-a-law.
